detailed_description: GIF Compressor re-encodes an animated GIF in the browser at a smaller pixel size. Upload a GIF, set the compression level slider (which here acts as a scale factor between 20% and 100% of the original width and height), optionally enable color reduction with a maximum color slider (16-256 in steps of 16) that biases the gif.js quality setting, then click Compress. Frames are parsed with gifuct-js, downscaled on a canvas, and re-encoded with gif.js using a Web Worker, producing a new GIF that can be previewed and downloaded with size and savings percentage shown. The tool does not pick lossy vs lossless modes, remove duplicate frames, change frame rate, strip metadata, or guarantee perceptual quality preservation.
usage_steps: Click the upload area and select an animated GIF
Drag the compression level slider between 20% and 100% to scale frame width and height
Optionally tick Reduce Colors and pick a max color count between 16 and 256 in steps of 16
Click Compress and wait while frames are decoded and re-encoded with gif.js
Compare the original and compressed previews side by side with size and savings percentage
Click Download to save the compressed GIF or Clear to start over
usage_examples: Shrink a screen recording GIF to half size so it fits a chat attachment limit
Re-encode an oversized hero GIF at 60% scale to lower the page weight before publishing
Use Reduce Colors to trade extra size savings against the slight color banding it introduces
Compare the original and compressed previews to decide whether the smaller file still looks acceptable
